hero.oneLiner: Bharat Gears is a 50+ year Indian precision gear manufacturer with deep bevel-gear grinding expertise, serving automotive, agriculture, construction, and EV segments globally.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Bharat Gears is a 50+ year Indian precision gear manufacturer with deep bevel-gear grinding expertise, serving automotive, agriculture, construction, and EV segments globally.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Bharat Gears Limited (BGL) manufactures high-quality precision-engineered gears, sub-assemblies/aggregates, heat-treatment furnaces, and automotive components. It caters to diverse industries including agriculture, construction equipment, commercial vehicles, and EVs, with a global presence across 14 countries. The company is the first independent Indian gear manufacturer to develop bevel gear grinding capabilities and operates the largest dry cutting facility in India.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Gears and Sub-assemblies:** Ring gears & pinions, Transmission gears, Shafts, Differential gears, Spiral & Hypoid Bevel Gears, Straight bevel gears, Axle shafts, Crown wheel & pinion, Fly-wheel assemblies and rings, Propeller shaft components, U-cross, Differential cages, Sub-assembly for higher-end tractor differential application, Ground Bevel gears
- **Furnaces:** High-end batch and continuous heating furnaces
- **Automotive Components:** Automotive clutch components, Turbochargers and components, Break lining, Centre & clutch bearing

certifications.title: Certs (RHP)
certifications.body:

- ISO 9001:2015 (Faridabad)
- ISO 14001:2015 (Faridabad, Lonand)
- ISO 45001:2018 (Faridabad, Lonand)
- OHSAS 18001 (Faridabad, historical)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Structural drivers such as increasing localisation, advanced technology adoption, rising demand for value-added and differentiated offerings and the growing shift towards aggregate and sub-assembly sourcing are creating new avenues of growth.
- Evolving mobility requirements are increasing demand across emerging EV segments.
- The 'China plus one strategy' continues to work in India's favour as major OEMs look at alternative supply bases to mitigate risk.
- Short-term headwinds could impact demand, but long-term opportunities remain strong on domestic and global fronts.
- Strong order pipeline, customer-first approach and commitment to continuous innovation will strengthen technology leadership and optimise costs.
- Backed by a strong order pipeline.
- Aggressive new order bookings supported by faster developments and a strong value proposition helped boost demand.
- Strong demand from the domestic farm equipment segment and aggressive new order acquisitions with leading farm equipment OEMs.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Operational excellence and cost leadership: strengthen processes to enhance productivity, quality and efficiency across the value chain while sharpening competitive edge.
- Profitable and disciplined growth: improve margins, return ratios and cash flows while scaling operations sustainably.
- Diversification of customer base and markets: expand into new customer segments, geographies and end-use applications to reduce concentration risks.
- Enhancing product and value proposition: move up the value chain through differentiated offerings, customisation and increasing the share of premium solutions.
- Technological and digital transformation: leverage automation, digital tools, data analytics and innovation to improve agility, scalability and decision-making.
- No explicit dividend policy, buyback, debt reduction, or reinvestment philosophy stated in the provided text.
- Corporate Social Responsibility: The Company has a statutory CSR obligation (amount required disclosed in Note 41), indicating a structural commitment to social spending, though specific targets or projects are not detailed in the provided text.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Capital expenditure for the year was largely funded through internal accruals. The Company strengthened its balance sheet and consolidated its Debt profile by making ₹13 crore principal repayment to term lenders. No specific new capacity expansion projects, plant commissioning timelines, or named capex programs are disclosed in the provided annual-report text.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- First independent Indian gear manufacturer to develop Bevel Gear Grinding capabilities, supporting EV and low-noise NVH applications
- Largest dry cutting facility in India with Industry 4.0 aligned infrastructure
- 50+ year legacy and deep technical expertise in bevel gears (face milling, face hobbing, Hypolfex) and cylindrical gears
- Long-standing technical collaboration with AFC-Holcroft, USA (since 1982) for furnace manufacturing
- Diversified customer base including prominent global OEMs (e.g., DANA Corporation, John Deere, Toyota, Ashok Leyland) across agriculture, construction, and commercial vehicles
- Comprehensive portfolio enabling forward integration into sub-assemblies and aggregates

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Customer concentration risk — One customer accounted for 10% or more of revenue, and 7 customers represented 44.27% of receivables, exposing the Company to significant financial loss if a major customer defaults or reduces orders.
- Foreign currency exchange rate risk — The Company has unhedged foreign currency receivables and payables in USD and EUR; a 5% adverse currency move could reduce profit before tax by approximately â¹239 lakhs, impacting earnings materially.
- Interest rate risk on variable-rate borrowings — A 100 basis point increase in interest rates would decrease profit by â¹86.44 lakhs due to exposure on floating-rate debt, which could pressure profitability if rates rise.
- Liquidity and refinancing risk — The Company relies on short-term borrowings and undrawn facilities; â¹6,949.97 lakhs of variable-rate debt matures within one year, requiring continuous access to banking lines and cash flow to avoid liquidity stress.
- Raw material price pass-through risk — While the Company states it passes raw material price variations to customers, an inability to do so promptly or fully during volatile commodity cycles could compress margins.
- Credit risk on trade receivables — No collateral is held against receivables, and impairment is assessed at each reporting date; a deterioration in customer credit quality could lead to unexpected write-offs.
- Operational leverage and fixed-cost absorption risk — Profitability improvement is partly attributed to higher volumes driving fixed-cost absorption; a downturn in tractor or export demand could reverse these gains and pressure EBITDA.
